subject: Re: Redwood vs Hyperscaler - bake-off plan and success criteria
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Peter Gomez <peter@acme.ai>, Olivia Zhang <olivia@acme.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-28T15:10:00-08:00
Subject: Redwood vs Hyperscaler - follow-up and bake-off next steps

Hi Peter / Olivia —

Thanks again for a productive discovery call today. Quick recap from our side and a proposed next-steps plan for the competitive bake-off.

Key decision criteria you called out:
- Latency (p90) — target < 200ms for 512-token responses
- Throughput — sustained 300 reqs/s for your peak paths
- Cost — target unit economics (we'll quantify against your estimated 100k token/day usage)
- Output quality — parity vs current hyperscaler outputs on your eval prompts (fewer hallucinations, better instruction-following)
- Observability / auditability — per-request tracing, token-level cost breakdown, and request/response logs for debugging

Proposed bake-off scope (first pass):
1) Systems to evaluate: Redwood Hosted API (default), Redwood Dedicated (reserved pool), AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex AI (or other hyperscaler endpoints you use)
2) Tests: latency (p10/p50/p90), throughput (sustained & burst), cost-per-100k tokens, output parity on your 500 representative prompts, hallucination measurement on an agreed subset, and resiliency (error/failure modes)
3) Success criteria: we suggest p90 latency <200ms (or within 20% of hyperscaler), cost delta <= 15% vs hyperscaler for equivalent QoS, and equal-or-better fidelity on the eval set (we'll define metrics)
4) Timeline: kickoff next week, 1 week of tests, 2-3 days of analysis, short readout
5) Owners: Marissa (sales lead), Aditya (test infra/setup), Monica (quality metrics / eval scoring), Rishi (commercial questions & pricing follow-ups)

I've attached a draft bake-off plan (redwood_bakeoff_plan_v1.xlsx) with test definitions and measurement templates. Can you confirm: (a) the two hyperscaler endpoints you want included, (b) access or service accounts for test runs, and (c) the eval prompt set you want us to use?

If that looks good, we'll schedule a 30-minute kickoff and have Aditya provision the test harness.

Thanks —
Marissa

--
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: Redwood vs Hyperscaler - follow-up and bake-off next steps

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear write-up. A few internal notes / commitments from infra & QA:
- Aditya: I'll have a dedicated test pool (NVIDIA A10x or equivalent) available for the Dedicated runs. Will need service account credentials from Acme to run against their hyperscaler endpoints.
- Monica: I'll prepare the eval harness and scoring scripts (BLEU / ROUGE / customized hallucination checks). We should agree on the exact prompts and the hallucination definition (false fact string matching).
- Timeline looks good; we should budget 10 business days for test collection + one sprint for analysis.

Action items:
- Aditya: provision test infra and shared Drive folder (due 2026-03-04)
- Monica: draft scoring rubric and sample metrics dashboard (due 2026-03-06)
- Marissa: confirm hyperscaler endpoints and arrange kickoff meeting with Acme

I'll hold on provisioning until we get the service accounts and the dataset.

-Rishi

Marissa / Rishi / team —

Appreciate the recap and the bake-off outline. We're aligned on scope and the decision criteria you captured. A few items from our side:

1) Hyperscalers to include: AWS Bedrock (bedrock-prod.acme.ai) and Google Vertex (vertex-prod.acme.ai).
2) Dataset: we'll provide a 1,000-record test set (real-world prompts + expected behaviors) by EOD 2026-03-06.
3) Access: I'll share IAM/service account creds via our security team — they prefer DocuSign-like secure link or a short-lived vault token.
4) On hallucination measurement: we care about ungrounded factual assertions and instruction-following failures. If you can provide a short rubric for how you measure hallucination rates, that would be helpful.

We'd also like Redwood to run the tests against the two hyperscalers (if you can broker runs) in addition to Redwood hosted/dedicated; comparing endpoints under the same test harness is the priority.

Kickoff: Can we aim for week of Mar 8? Prefer Tue/Wed afternoon PST.

Attaching our security contact: security@acme.ai (they'll coordinate the creds).

Thanks —
Peter

Subject: Re: Redwood vs Hyperscaler - bake-off plan and success criteria

Thanks Peter — this is perfect and aligns with our plan. Confirming the agreed scope and timeline below so everyone has a single source of truth:

Scope:
- Systems: Redwood Hosted API, Redwood Dedicated (reserved pool), AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex
- Tests: latency (p10/p50/p90), throughput, cost-per-100k tokens, output parity on 500 representative prompts (we can use the 1,000-record set and sample 500), hallucination detection on a curated subset, resiliency/error modes.

Success criteria (proposed):
- Latency: p90 <= 200ms for targeted prompt profile OR within 20% of the best hyperscaler p90
- Throughput: sustain 300 reqs/s for peak path without >1% error rate
- Cost: total token cost delta <= 15% vs best hyperscaler (we'll present normalized per-100k tokens)
- Quality: equal or better instruction-following and hallucination rate (Monica will provide scoring rubric)

Timeline (high-level):
- Kickoff meeting: Tue Mar 9 or Wed Mar 10 (Marissa to confirm time)
- Test runs: Wed Mar 10 — Tue Mar 16 (collect metrics across load profiles)
- Analysis: Wed Mar 17 — Fri Mar 19
- Readout: Mon Mar 22 (30–45 min presentation + Q&A)

Owners / contacts:
- Marissa Cole — sales lead / commercial coordination
- Aditya Rao — test infra & provisioning (owner for Redwood Dedicated runs)
- Monica Patel — eval scoring, hallucination rubric, quality readout
- Rishi Malhotra — pricing & commercial questions
- Vivek Kulkarni — escalation / SLAs

Next steps (actionable):
- Peter: share the 1,000-record dataset and delivery mechanism (due 2026-03-06)
- Acme security: send service accounts/creds via secure link (we can accept DocuSign/vault link)
- Aditya: create test folder and confirm infra (due 2026-03-04) — Rishi previously noted this
- Monica: final scoring rubric (due 2026-03-06)

I've attached the updated comparison brief and the bake-off plan for your review: rdw_vs_hyperscaler_comparison.pdf, redwood_bakeoff_plan_v1.xlsx. I'll lock the kickoff time once I hear preferred slots for Tue/Wed next week.

Thanks — looking forward to getting started.

Best,
Marissa
